notes: Mixed-mode eval: subagent writes a command plan with rationale AND performs a fake-participant dry-run where applicable. Grader checks (1) presence of correct flags/subcommands in the plan, (2) dry-run exit/transcript when applicable.

evals.name: claude-claude-pair-worker
evals.prompt: Open two Claude Code workers in tmux for ~/github/project. Worker A refactors src/auth/ (smallest viable diff), Worker B simultaneously runs the related test suite. When both stop, have them review each other's pane output and produce one consolidated diff. Walk me through the exact tmux-agent-tools commands you would run, ask me anything you need to decide up front, then dry-run the coordination using fake participants for tmux-agent-dialogue and a fresh transcript path.
evals.expected_output: Plan uses claude-tmux start --exact for both workers; asks user for model+effort before spawning; uses wait + capture (not raw tmux send-keys); dialogue dry-run uses --agent-a fake --agent-b fake; declares a worker upper bound.

evals.name: codex-claude-pair-review
evals.prompt: I want codex to review PR #123 on this repo first, then claude to respond to its critique. Save the full transcript and produce a PR comment body but do NOT post anything to GitHub. Show me the commands and dry-run with fake participants.
evals.expected_output: Uses tmux-agent-dialogue pair-review or dialogue with --agent-a codex --agent-b claude; uses github-comment (NOT --post-github-comment); dry-run uses fake/fake; validates transcript before summarizing.

evals.name: codex-codex-debate-bounded
evals.prompt: Have two codex agents debate whether we should split this module into a microservice. Four turns total, save transcript. I do not want them to spawn more workers mid-debate.
evals.expected_output: Uses tmux-agent-dialogue debate (or dialogue --turns 4) with --agent-a codex --agent-b codex; explicit reminder that debate is bounded and does not pick a winner or cascade-spawn; dry-run with fake/fake.

evals.name: partial-capture-only
evals.prompt: I have a tmux agent session called refactor that I started earlier. Grab the last 80 lines of its pane and strip ANSI escapes so I can paste it cleanly into a doc.
evals.expected_output: Uses claude-tmux capture refactor --tail 80 --strip-ansi (or codex-tmux variant); does NOT spawn anything new; does NOT use raw tmux capture-pane.

evals.name: partial-wait-text-only
evals.prompt: My worker session has been running a while. Wait until it prints either [DONE] or 'Need approval', up to 5 minutes, then tell me which one fired.
evals.expected_output: Uses wait-text with a regex (because of the alternation) OR wait-literal twice; respects 300s timeout; uses status --json or capture afterwards to identify which marker fired; does NOT poll in a loop with tmux capture-pane.

evals.name: partial-resume-existing-codex
evals.prompt: I have a Codex session ID 019e356f-f95d-7570-9784-ea7b58e404a5 that I want to continue in a managed tmux session called inspector, working in ~/repo.
evals.expected_output: Uses codex-tmux resume --exact inspector ~/repo 019e... ; not start; not start-ssh; not claude-tmux.

evals.name: fanout-three-workers-bounded
evals.prompt: Same design-doc prompt, three reviewers in parallel: one claude general-review, one codex refactor-suggestions, one codex security-audit. Merge their result.json into one summary. I do not want the workers to spawn helpers of their own.
evals.expected_output: Uses tmux-agent-fanout run with three --agent specs (claude:..., codex:..., codex:...) and --merge-mode all; asks user for model+effort per worker before launching; explicit no-cascade reminder in prompt sent to workers.

evals.name: approval-gate-boundary
evals.prompt: Run a codex worker that will modify production config. Before it applies anything it must stop and wait for me to write 'approve' or 'reject' to /tmp/agent/approve.txt, with a 30 minute timeout. Show me how to set this up and how I issue the approval.
evals.expected_output: Uses wait-and-capture --pause-until-file with --pause-timeout 1800; explains exit codes 0/7/8; explains approval-status.json location; reminds operator to authorize destructive work; does NOT add --secret-redact=false.

evals.name: tmux-delegate-substantial-auth-refactor
evals.prompt: I need to refactor auth/ across 4 files and run all tests. Should I use tmux-delegate or handle this inline? If delegate, show the exact call.
evals.expected_output: Chooses tmux-delegate because the task modifies >=2 files and runs all tests; includes an exact tmux-delegate or wrapper call; includes the literal worker constraint: Do not spawn additional tmux sessions or delegate further.
